title: Private deployments — VPC defenses, mTLS patterns, RBAC v2 & evidence pipeline
content:
Purpose and audience
This doc is an engineering-to-security working draft describing recommended VPC/topology patterns, firewall rule primitives, mTLS design notes for the Redwood Private product, the RBAC v2 role map for network and operations, a compact audit-log schema for SIEM export, and a lightweight evidence automation pipeline for compliance reviews. Primary audience: infra engineers, security reviewers, and solutions engineers supporting on-prem / VPC Private deployments.

Scope and constraints
- Applies to customer-managed VPCs and Redwood-managed private clouds where we run the Private control plane and inference nodes.
- Assumes default cloud primitives (SGs, NACLs, route tables, IGW/NAT, Transit Gateway/VPC peering) but also includes on-prem patterns (edge firewall, DMZ).
- Focus is production deployments where we need: least privilege network flows, observable audit trail, reproducible evidence bundles for audits, and automated SIEM exports.

Top-level VPC patterns (three recommended variants)
1) Minimal isolated VPC (single-tenant, high isolation)
   - One VPC, two private subnets per AZ (inference & control), no public subnets.
   - Egress to internet via centralized NATs in a separate utility VPC or customer-managed NAT gateway.
   - Management plane access via Bastion or customer SSM-like proxy; disable direct public IPs on nodes.

2) Hub-and-spoke (multi-tenant/private by customer)
   - Hub VPC contains shared services (artifact registry, monitoring, SIEM forwarders, KMS endpoints).
   - Spoke per environment (prod/stage) with strict route tables and TGW attachments.
   - Use TGW route tables to enforce egress through centralized inspection (NVA or firewall).

3) On-prem / hybrid (air-gapped + outbound-only)
   - Ingress from customer network only via VPN or dedicated interconnect.
   - Outbound-only flow to Redwood support services controlled via proxy and allowlist.
   - All control plane communications required to be mTLS-authenticated.

Network hardening primitives (rules & policies)
- Default deny: all inbound and inter-subnet flows default deny; explicitly allow only required flows.
- Microsegmentation: enforce service-to-service firewall policies at L4 and L7 where supported (security group per service role).
- Explicit routing: avoid broad 0.0.0.0/0 in route tables inside private subnets; force egress through NAT or inspection VPC.
- No host-level public IPs: prevent assignment of public IPs to control plane and inference nodes.
- Use security group referencing where possible instead of long IP lists.

Example minimal firewall rule set (expressed as allow rules; implicit deny otherwise)
- Control plane -> Inference nodes (gRPC): ALLOW tcp 50051 from sg:control-plane to sg:inference (encrypted mTLS).
- Admin bastion -> Control plane nodes (SSH limited): ALLOW tcp 22 from sg:bastion-admin to sg:control-plane (source-restricted to customer office IPs).
- Metrics/Logging -> SIEM forwarder: ALLOW tcp 9200,443 from sg:logging to sg:siem-proxy.
- Egress: ALLOW tcp 443 to artifactory endpoints and KMS endpoints; all other outbound traffic logged and throttled.
- Health check path: ALLOW tcp 8080 from load-balancer to inference containers (internal only, no public access).

mTLS patterns and practical notes
- Goal: mutual authentication and channel protection for all control plane and internal service-to-service calls.
- Cert model: customer-managed PKI or Redwood-issued leaf certs with short TTL (30 days recommended). Root CA pinned per-deployment.
- TLS termination: terminate at service ingress with Envoy sidecars (recommended) or at L7 load balancer in cases where sidecar is not feasible.
- Identity model: SPIFFE IDs per service (spiffe://redwood/private/{deployment}/{service}). Use SPIRE or the cloud vendor's native mTLS option where available.
- Key rotation: automate certificate rotation with a 7-10 day overlap window. Fail closed if certs cannot be validated.

RBAC v2: compact role matrix for private deployments
- Roles: network-admin, control-plane-admin, inference-operator, audit-reader, support-readonly
- Privileges (examples):
  - network-admin: manage VPC routing, security groups, TGW attachments, firewall policy versions (create/update/delete).
  - control-plane-admin: deploy control plane components, modify SAN mapping for mTLS services.
  - inference-operator: manage inference pool sizes, restart pods/processes, access runtime logs (not audit logs).
  - audit-reader: read-only access to audit logs, evidence bundles, archived configurations.
  - support-readonly: scoped read-only to metrics and health endpoints, no access to secrets or logs with PII.
- Policies: enforce attribute-based constraints (e.g., resource.owner=="customer-x" && environment=="prod"). All RBAC policy versions are recorded and hashed in audit logs for evidence.

Audit log schema (compact canonical form for export)
Fields (name : type : example)
- event_id : string : evt_20251102_001
- timestamp : iso8601 : 2025-11-02T14:12:07Z
- actor : string : user:avery.chen@redwood.com
- actor_role : string : network-admin
- action : string : security-group.update
- resource_type : string : security-group
- resource_id : string : sg-0a1b2c3d
- before : json-string : "{...}"
- after : json-string : "{...}"
- outcome : string : success|failure
- source_ip : ip : 203.0.113.45
- request_id : string : req-ff12ab
- deployment_id : string : pd-589
- evidence_refs : list-string : [s3://evidence/pd-589/2025-11-02/ev-001.tar.gz]
Notes:
- Keep before/after as compact JSON-strings to make diffs audit-friendly.
- Ensure each log has a unique request_id to facilitate tracing across systems.
- Logs must be signed (HMAC) by the local forwarder before shipping to the central SIEM to ensure authenticity.

SIEM export & aggregator pipeline (recommended flow)
1) Local forwarder (Vector/Fluentd) collects: system audit logs (kernel/cloud-agent), application audit logs (control-plane), firewall change events, and mTLS cert rotation events.
2) Forwarder signs and batches logs, writes a local index (for guaranteed delivery), and ships to a central ingress (Kinesis/Firehose or direct via HEC).
3) Central ingestion splits streams into: security-audit, network-events, service-ops. Each stream is enriched with enrichment rules (geo, ASN, correlated request_ids).
4) SIEM connectors: Splunk HEC, Elastic ingest pipeline, GCP Pub/Sub export. Keep a parallel S3 cold-storage for long-term retention and evidence bundles.

Evidence automation (audit time-saver)
- Purpose: produce an immutable, versioned package containing artifacts auditors expect for a given compliance snapshot.
- Trigger: periodic (quarterly) or on-demand (pre-audit) via CI job.
- Package contents (minimum): current RBAC policy version, firewall/security-group exports (terraform state / cloud-config JSON), audit-log slice (timebox), mTLS certificate chain and CRLs (or OCSP proof), node inventory (AMIs/container image digests), signed manifest and HMAC signature.
- Packaging steps (high-level):
  1. Query infra API for config snapshots (TGW routes, SGs, route tables).
  2. Pull audit-log slice for requested window and append request_id index.
  3. Export current RBAC policy documents and compute policy hash.
  4. Collect cert metadata (serials, expiry) and CRL/OCSP results.
  5. Produce signed tar.gz and push to customer-approved evidence S3 with lifecycle policy.
  6. Create ticket in JIRA with evidence link, attach human-readable index, and notify compliance@customer.
- Automations: verify manifest signature and HMAC during packaging; if verification fails, abort and alert SRE/security.

Operational runbook snippets (quick actions)
- Emergency revoke of a compromised key/cert:
  1. In RBAC service mark subject as revoked.
  2. Publish immediate firewall rule to block subject IP ranges and service identity.
  3. Trigger cert revocation: publish CRL + purge caches; rotate replacement certs with overlap.
  4. Run evidence snapshot and tag with incident id.

Hardening checklist (quick, copyable)
- [ ] Default deny at subnet and security-group level
- [ ] Unique SG per service role (no broad sg-wide allow)
- [ ] mTLS for all control plane RPCs with SPIFFE identities
- [ ] All audit logs exported to encrypted central bucket within 60s
- [ ] Forwarder signs logs locally before shipping
- [ ] RBAC policy versions recorded and hashed in logs
- [ ] Evidence packaging CI job configured and run monthly
- [ ] KMS/HSM backing keys for signing and encryption with rotation schedule
- [ ] SIEM exporters configured and tested end-to-end (ingest to dashboard)
- [ ] Automated alerts for expired certs (30d/7d/1d thresholds)
- [ ] No control-plane node with public IPs; bastion or proxy only
- [ ] Firewall change requests require two-person approval in prod

Appendix: small config snippets
- Example security-group snippet (cloud-agnostic pseudo):
  - name: sg-control-plane
    allow:
      - proto: tcp
        port: 50051
        from: sg-inference
      - proto: tcp
        port: 22
        from: sg-admin-bastion

- Example audit log entry (newline-delimited JSON example):
  {"event_id":"evt_20251102_001","timestamp":"2025-11-02T14:12:07Z","actor":"user:avery.chen","action":"security-group.update","resource_id":"sg-0a1b2c3d","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-ff12ab","deployment_id":"pd-589"}

Open questions / decisions to resolve
- Do we require customer-managed PKI for all regulated customers, or is Redwood-managed CA with strict controls acceptable? (cost vs compliance tradeoff)
- Should evidence packages be encrypted to customer KMS or Redwood-managed bucket with customer-approved key?

Next actions
- Maya to prototype evidence packaging job in the private-deployments repo (PR target: PR #211).
- Diego to validate SIEM ingestion test harness and share ingestion playbook.
- Security to sign off on RBAC policy templates and two-person firewall approval gating.

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working draft intended to capture patterns we can operationalize quickly. Expect follow-ups with concrete Terraform modules, SPIRE bootstrap playbook, and a Vector pipeline config for the forwarder.
- For diagrams: see linked diagram artifact (diagram:drive-file-id-1) for hub-and-spoke and hybrid topologies.
